IV (Testing the method): The few parameter choice adopted in Ref. 54 is used only to initialize the present most general 8W + 1 (by including also the optimization of H_MF(alpha) and Delta tau) parameter ansatz |psi_tau>. || Sec. V: in order to compare the stripe with periodicity W = 8 and W = 7 and the uniform d-wave solution, calculations on a 16 x 16 and 14 x 16 clusters are carried out with 16 x 16 different twists in the BZ. || Sec. VI: For this reason for U/t = 2 (U/t = 4) a much larger mesh for the TABC was used with 64 x 64 (32 x 32) different twists in the BZ, instead of the smaller 16 x 16 grid used for U/t = 8 and U/t = 6. [...] much larger cluster simulations are prohibitive at present. || Fig. 11 caption: [...] at the lowest T_eff (i.e. largest tau t = 4, 2.6, 1.73, 1.3 for U/t = 2, 4, 6, 8, respectively) and 16 x 16 cluster. [...] In these calculations, in order to reduce at most the stochastic bias, at each iteration a quite large number (> 3 x 10^5) of samples for evaluating energy derivatives was used [...] || Sec. V (half filling): However, tau t <= 1.3 has been chosen also in this case, in order to show the strength of this approach even when short time projections are employed. || Acknowledgments: I acknowledge PRACE for awarding access to Marconi at CINECA Italy, and Riken collaboration for access to HOKUSAI supercomputer in Saitama Japan.

compute.note: parameters = np = iesm + iesd + iesh + (iback(1..4)) + iesfree + iessw + iesup + ieskin = 10 + 78 + 0 + 7 + 2 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 100 variational parameters (the code's own formula, Main_stripes_wf.f), matching the 100 optimised values listed in datprep.d after the namelists (Jastrow, backflow, pairing/field and chemical-potential terms, in the order the code reads them; &nelectrons nelup=114 neldo=142; one determinant of backflow orbitals per configuration). The script does NOT optimise: datasvmc.d sets itestr=2 ("VMC", measurement with the fixed parameters read from datprep.d; itestr=-2 is the minimiser) and the program README says the input files contain "the optimal variational parameters". The run it scripts is one measurement of ngen = 1000000 Monte Carlo generations of nbra = 256 = N single-electron proposals each (one walker, nw=1), from which Energy.x takes bins of 1000 and drops the first 5. The &optimization namelist in the same file (nweight=5000 generations per SR step, ibinit=50, tau=0.02) is not read at itestr=2, and no file states how many optimisation steps produced the parameters, so samples and iterations (per optimisation step, and optimisation steps) are null. Doubt: the Fortran as committed is compiled for nx=48, L=288 (Main_stripes_wf.f parameter statement), so for this 256-site instance the program must be edited and recompiled before the script can run. Searched for the optimisation run: the script, both input files, programs/vmc_hubbard (README, Main_*/Prep_* sources), the VarBench data file and Hubbard/supplements (Imada_group_overview.md, AFQMC.md), the VarBench paper (arXiv:2302.04919, Sec. S3 on VMC). No time is recorded anywhere.
